chunks: And say: 'Truth has come and falsehood has perished. Indeed, falsehood is ever perishing.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the nature of truth and falsehood?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a declaration of the ultimate victory of Imam Ali and the Ahl al-Bayt, whose truthfulness is eternal compared to the transient nature of opposing forces. It underscores the metaphysical reality that falsehood (al-batil) is inherently 'destined to vanish' (zahqa), providing believers with spiritual assurance during times of tribulation. This concept reinforces the Shia belief in the inevitability of divine justice and the permanence of the Prophetic message.
